The warrior inhaled sharply, it was his only tell that a strike was imminent and his body became electrified from the sound, the roar, of the cool breeze blasting past his teeth. They had trained him to be quick and to be fierce, but also to be silent and never give the prey a warning they didn't deserve. That was his people's way, to become one with the night, with the shadows, to hide and to never be seen until it was far, far too late.

Any true warrior would have sprang back and met him with equal ferocity and he would deserve the misery in that challenge; poisoning the ambush was truly disgraceful.

Except... That wasn't what happened. When he left the bushes the prey did not turn, it did not raise it's ferocious weapons, it did not bare claws, hackles, horn or tooth. All it did was continue plodding along like some sort of fat beast, barely intelligent enough to breathe and munch on whatever slop it was forcing down it's ugly gullet. Disgusting. They were all disgusting beasts, but he knew well they were sentient creatures. When they came from the sky the people scrambled to defend against the terrible invaders who arrived in gleaming ships of metal, each one a great ark from beyond the long night that gripped his northern home.

His people came from many generations of warriors, his people stretched back to a tribe that came north to settle the harsh land and they fought constantly since those days. All throughout his childhood his people had sang of great conquerors and adventurers who squared off against nature itself.

Somehow this noble lineage had produced a whelp that failed to adhere to his training, a clumsy fool who sprang from the bush with his spear the wrong way!

Perhaps that was why his first strike missed, the invader deftly avoided the thrust and before a rebound could happen it had taken control of the weapon. Obviously a creature that size had power, immense power that the warrior could not have matched even if he had been showered in supernatural strength by the gods. This creature was incredible, it's figure was clad in hard plates that overlapped and easily overcame even the stoutest of kicks! Ignoring the pain the warrior rebounded to plant another blow to the creature's mighty, bulbous eye with his fist.

Ponk!

At first there was no pain, just the sensation of the impact on his knuckles. Yet he knew it had ended poorly for him, the bland sensation slid away off his nerves to reveal a growing heat, a fire inside his flesh that heralded agony! Despite his excitement the pain told him his fingers were severely wounded, it was as if the creature's eye was made of some type of golden stone polished smooth. Damn them! Damn those invaders, even without the advanced technology and weapons that conjured lightning at will they were invincible!

He wouldn't go down without a fight.

They wouldn't beat him. They wouldn't enslave him either, like so many others of his kind, putting him behind walls of metal.

His spear was lost, the creature tossed it aside like it was a piece of kindling, so the warrior dropped his fur cloak and found a branch heavy enough to swing. That would be his final weapon, and he gave it a mighty pull to free it from the fallen sentinel that once reached with green needles toward the sky. Undeterred the creature advanced on him with a quickened pace, it's hefty girth did not make it slow and he only imagined that beneath it's scaly hide were incredible muscles!

The warrior steeled himself and sprang forward again, striking the creature in the knee with a mighty blow. Even that wasn't enough to bring it down, it just merely dropped to a kneel and brought up an arm to block the second strike. Had they not been mortal enemies he would have appreciated his opponent's speed, but he only had malice in his heart to keep the terror at bay. He held on to his courage, his remaining honor, his people's honor, depended on him fighting to the bitter end.

Meanwhile the invader had other plans, it's stubby fingers reached out with surprising nimbleness and groped at the warrior. Thankfully he was quick and evidently slippery enough to keep his opponent's grip from finding no purchase on his arm, and a good thing too since it obviously could have crushed it instantly. He swung again and struck the creature in the head, the stubby nodule didn't turn or rebound off the "club" but he knew it was a good blow!

Had the fight ended there he would have felt satisfied and honored the creature with a quick death, but all he managed to do was to anger the foul beast. What wounds he did inflict were minor, just cosmetic to the tough plates that kept the invader safe, and it belched a vile liquid all over itself as it lunged for him.

That time the warrior was not so swift, because with the lunge came a hot lance of pain that sliced through him.

Falling to his knees he saw the invader had struck him with it's lighting stick, a gentle tck-tck-tck was all he heard before it was pressed to his skull...

...

...

Taylor heaved and tossed the writhing alien up on the processing table, bound and gagged, and helped hold the fighting creature down. They had done it probably a thousand times before, and Hawthorne was ready with a syringe.

"Aww, goodnight... Shhh," she cooed, petting it's head with a gloved hand. "This one looks male, I guess we'll put him with the others...?"

"Shit, fine by me. Bastard knocked open the coolant hose on my suit though, looks like stuffing rags next to it didn't work."

She looked up at him with unsympathetic eyes and said, "Bill. Come on. Go get it fixed."

"Fine, fine," he sighed, stepping back, "any word from-"

"Oh! Yeah, they want you down south to the other collection area. Comet predictions have come back in and it looks like the timetable has moved up."

Much like the indigenous people, the comet didn't want to cooperate and redirection attempts had failed; it was up to the ground team to save as many as they could before it arrived.

He shrugged and ducked out through the hatch.
